facts.text: India's internal challenges include separatist movements, issues of north-east India, naxalism, communalism and regionalism.
facts.quote: We shall see some internal challenges like separatist movements, issues of north-east India, naxalism, communalism and regionalism.

facts.text: Akali Dal was the major political party in Punjab; in 1973 it passed the 'Aanandpur Sahib Resolution'.
facts.quote: Akali Dal was the major political party in Punjab. In 1973, the Akali Dal passed the 'Aanandpur Sahib Resolution'.

facts.text: The resolution demanded that Chandigarh be made part of Punjab, Punjabi speaking parts of other States be included in Punjab, recruitment of Sikhs in the army be increased, and Punjab get more autonomy.
facts.quote: Chandigarh should be made part of Punjab, the Punjabi speaking parts in other States should be included in the State of Punjab, recruitment of Sikhs in the Indian army should be increased, and more autonomy should be given to the State of Punjab.

facts.text: Akali Dal came to power in Punjab in 1977 and asked for a larger share of river waters for Punjab and 'holy city' status for Amritsar.
facts.quote: Akali Dal came to power in Punjab in 1977. While taking charge, they asked for a larger share of river waters for Punjab, 'holy city' status for Amritsar, etc. along with their old demands.

facts.text: In 1980 the movement for 'Independent Khalistan' took root in Punjab.
facts.quote: In 1980, the movement for 'Independent Khalistan' took root in Punjab.

facts.text: The leader of the Akali Dal then was Sant Harcharan Singh Longowal, who directed his activists from the Golden Temple to stage protests.
facts.quote: During that period, the leader of the Akali Dal was Sant Harcharan Singh Longowal. He used to direct his activists from the Golden Temple to stage protests.

facts.text: Armed followers gathered around the staunch Khalistan supporter Sant Jarnailsingh Bhindranwale, and terrorist activities began.
facts.quote: armed followers started gathering around the staunch Khalistan supporter Sant Jarnailsingh Bhindranwale. During that period, terrorist activities had begun.

facts.text: Bhindranwale was arrested in 1981, accused of the murder of newspaper editor Lala Jagatnarayan.
facts.quote: Bhindranwale was arrested in 1981, accused of the murder of newspaper editor, Lala Jagatnarayan.

facts.text: President's rule was imposed in Punjab in 1983.
facts.quote: Due to these developments, President's rule was imposed in Punjab in 1983.

facts.text: Bhindranwale went to stay at a religious place called Akal Takht; his followers captured the Golden Temple and built a barricade of sand bags, so the area looked like a fort.
facts.quote: Bhindranwale went to stay at a religious place called Akal Takht. Bhindranwale's followers captured the Golden Temple and built a barricade of sand bags over there. The area looked like a fort.

facts.text: The main task of getting the terrorists out of the Golden Temple was entrusted to Major General Kuldeep Singh Brar.
facts.quote: The main task of getting the terrorists out of the Golden Temple was entrusted to Major General Kuldeep Singh Brar.

facts.text: Operation Blue Star started on the morning of 3rd June 1984 and ended on 6th June; the army functioned with great restraint; it ended with the death of Bhindranwale and other terrorists.
facts.quote: On the morning of 3rd June 1984, the mission 'Operation Blue Star' started. The Operation ended on 6th June. In this military operation, the Indian army functioned with great restraint. The operation ended with the death of Bhindranwale and other terrorists.

facts.text: In 1986 another operation against terrorists in the Golden Temple, 'Operation Black Thunder', was conducted; after it the establishment of peace in Punjab picked up momentum.
facts.quote: In 1986, an operation had to be conducted against terrorists in the Golden Temple once more. It was called 'Operation Black Thunder'. After this action was taken, the process of establishment of peace in Punjab picked up momentum.

facts.text: A military expedition taken up with a particular objective is called an operation.
facts.quote: A military expedition taken up with a particular objective is called an operation. Operation Blue Star was an operation undertaken to evict the terrorists hiding in the Golden Temple.

facts.text: North-east India consists of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura; these States differ in ethnicity, language and culture.
facts.quote: North-east India consists of the eight States of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura. ... These States are different with respect to ethnicity, language and cultural diversity.

facts.text: The first Prime Minister of independent India took the lead in bringing the tribes of these areas into the mainstream.
facts.quote: The first Prime Minister of independent India took the lead in bringing the tribes living in these areas into the mainstream of the country.

facts.text: In 1954 Nehru formed the North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA) area, comprising territories on the Sino-Indian border and tribal areas north of Assam.
facts.quote: In 1954, he formed the North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA) area, comprising of the territories on the Sino-Indian border and the tribal areas towards the north of Assam.

facts.text: Nehru aimed to develop the tribes while preserving their culture; special provisions for these areas are in the VI Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
facts.quote: Nehru took the position of bringing about the development of hundreds of tribes in these parts while preserving their culture. Special provisions have been made with respect to these areas in the VI Schedule of the Indian Constitution.

facts.text: In 1965 the responsibility of administering the NEFA area was given to the Ministry of External Affairs.
facts.quote: In 1965, the responsibility of administering this area was given to the Ministry of External Affairs.

facts.text: The Northeastern Council Act of 1971 was to advise the Central Government on common economic and social matters, inter-state transport, electricity, flood control, etc.
facts.quote: The Northeastern Council Act of 1971 was supposed to advise the Central Government regarding aspects of common interest in economic and social spheres, inter-state transport, electricity, flood control, etc.

facts.text: When India became independent, the government gave administrative autonomy to the Mizo majority districts of the Lushai hills.
facts.quote: When India became independent, the government gave administrative autonomy to the districts of Mizo majority areas of the Lushai hills.

facts.text: When the States Reorganisation Commission was appointed in 1953, Mizo leaders started demanding an autonomous 'Mizo' province.
facts.quote: When the States Reorganisation Commission was appointed in 1953, the expectations of the people in this area grew. Mizo leaders started demanding an autonomous 'Mizo' province.

facts.text: In 1959 Mizoram experienced severe drought; during this famine Mizo leader Laldenga served the common people a lot.
facts.quote: In 1959 the territory of Mizoram experienced severe drought. During this famine, Mizo leader Laldenga served the common people a lot.

facts.text: In 1961 Laldenga established the Mizo National Front (MNF) and asked for 'Greater Mizoram' carved out of Tripura, Manipur and Mizo majority areas of the Lushai hills.
facts.quote: In 1961, Laldenga established an organisation called Mizo National Front (MNF). He asked for 'Greater Mizoram', an independent nation carved out of Tripura, Manipur and Mizo majority areas from the Lushai hills.

facts.text: In March 1966 the MNF announced the emergence of Independent Mizoram; Prime Minister Indira Gandhi handled the situation firmly and suppressed the rebellion.
facts.quote: In March 1966, Mizo National Front announced the emergence of Independent Mizoram. Prime Minister Indira Gandhi handled the situation firmly and suppressed the rebellion.

facts.text: When the situation calmed down in 1972, the Mizo majority area was given the status of a Union Territory.
facts.quote: When the situation calmed down in 1972, the Mizo majority area was given the status of a Union Territory.

facts.text: In 1985 Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi had an agreement with the MNF; Mizoram became a full-fledged State and Laldenga became Chief Minister.
facts.quote: In 1985, Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi had an agreement with the Mizo National Front and Mizoram was given the status of a full-fledged State. Laldenga became the Chief Minister of the State.

facts.text: The Naga tribe is known as a martial tribe and settled in the Eastern Himalayas, the Naga hills and border areas of Assam and Myanmar.
facts.quote: The Naga tribe in north-east India is known as a martial tribe. The Naga tribe had settled in Eastern Himalayas, the Naga hills, border areas of Assam and Myanmar.

facts.text: In 1946 some educated Naga youth established the Naga National Council (NNC), which later demanded an independent State of Nagaland under Angami Zapu Fizo.
facts.quote: In 1946, some educated Naga youth established an organisation called Naga National Council (NNC). Later they made a demand for an independent State of Nagaland. They were led by Angami Zapu Fizo.

facts.text: In 1954 the Naga National Council announced the establishment of an independent federation of Nagaland.
facts.quote: In 1954, the Naga National Council announced the establishment of an independent federation of Nagaland.

facts.text: In 1955 skirmishes happened between local Nagas and soldiers of the Assam Rifles; military action was taken to suppress them.
facts.quote: In 1955, skirmishes happened between local Nagas and the soldiers of the Assam Rifles. Military action was taken to suppress the skirmishes.

facts.text: The Naga majority territory was first made a Union Territory; Nagaland became a full-fledged State on 1st December 1963 from the Naga majority territory and part of Tuensang.
facts.quote: Central Government decided to give the Naga majority territory the status of a Union Territory. Nagaland was made a full-fledged State on 1st December 1963 by putting together the Naga majority territory and part of Tuensang.

facts.text: In 1983 the All Assam Students Union and Assam Ganasangram Parishad staged an intense agitation over the dominance of Bengali migrants in Assam.
facts.quote: In 1983, there was an intense agitation staged by All Assam Students Union and Assam Ganasangram Parishad over the question of the dominance in Assam of Bengali migrants.

facts.text: In 1985 Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, Central Home Minister Shankarrao Chavan and Assamese leader Prafullakumar Mohanto signed an Accord to send infiltrated Bangladeshi citizens back.
facts.quote: In 1985, Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, Central Home Minister Shankarrao Chavan and Assamese leader Prafullakumar Mohanto signed an Accord. It was decided to send the Bangladeshi citizens who had infiltrated in Assam back to their original places.

facts.text: In 1986 Assam Legislative Assembly elections were held and Prafullakumar Mohanto of the Asom Ganaparishad became Chief Minister; peace was established through this democratic process.
facts.quote: In 1986, elections were held for Assam Legislative Assembly and Prafullakumar Mohanto, of the Asom Ganaparishad became the new Chief Minister. Due to this democratic process, it became possible to establish peace in Assam.

facts.text: NEFA was created in 1954; in 1972 it began to be called Arunachal Pradesh (region of the rising sun); on 20th February 1987 it got the status of a constituent State.
facts.quote: In 1954, NEFA was created. In 1972, it began to be called Arunachal Pradesh (region of the rising sun). On 20th February 1987, it got the status of a constituent State.

facts.text: From 1960 to 2000 North-east India progressed towards a more matured democracy, through industrialisation and spread of education.
facts.quote: During the period from 1960 to 2000, North-east India has progressed towards a more matured democracy. This area is on the path of progress through industrialisation, spread of education, etc.

facts.text: The Naxalite movement started at Naxalbari in Darjeeling district, West Bengal; in 1967 the Naxalites took charge of lands, put up red flags and declared the area free territory.
facts.quote: This movement started at Naxalbari in Darjeeling district in West Bengal. The Naxalites organised the small land holding farmers and land labourers and took charge of their lands, put up red flags and declared that area as free territory in 1967.

facts.text: The movement aimed to raise a voice against exploitation of farmers by landlords and to distribute landlords' land among tenants; later it strayed into terrorism and a parallel system, becoming a serious challenge to internal security.
facts.quote: The movement had the objectives of establishing Action Committees to raise a voice against the exploitation of the farmers by the landlords and confiscate the land of the landlords and distribute it among the tenants. Later, the movement strayed away from its objectives. ... This made Naxalism a serious challenge to India's internal security.

facts.text: The movement, mainly in West Bengal, spread to places like East Godavari, Karimnagar, Bastar, Sukma, Gadchiroli, Bhandara, Balaghat and Koraput.
facts.quote: The movement was mainly located in West Bengal. Later the movement spread to East Godavari in Andhra Pradesh, ... Karimnagar in Telangana, ... Bastar, Rajnandangaon and Sukma in Chhattisgarh, Gadchiroli, Bhandara ... Balaghat and Mandala in Madhya Pradesh and Koraput in Odisha.

facts.text: To maintain their influence, the Naxalites established the People's Liberation Guerilla Army (PLGA).
facts.quote: In order to maintain their influence, the Naxalites established an organisation called People's Liberation Guerilla Army (PLGA).

facts.text: Communalism is a serious threat to unity; it emerges out of narrow religious pride; the British sowed its seeds; excessive pride turns into bigotry and religious fanaticism.
facts.quote: Communalism is a serious threat to the unity of our country. Communalism emerges out of narrow religious pride. The British sowed the seeds of communalism in our country. ... But when this pride becomes excessive, then it turns into bigotry. ... This leads to religious fanaticism.

facts.text: Fanaticism is the base of communalism; it makes one oblivious of national interest and leads to distrust and riots.
facts.quote: Fanaticism is the base of communalism. It makes one oblivious of national interest. People of different religions don't trust each other.

facts.text: Trust between people is the basis of coexistence; to counter communalism we should mix with people of different religions, look at economic and social problems rationally and not mix them with religion.
facts.quote: Trust between people is the basis of coexistence. ... For this we should mix with people of different religions. We should accept the good practices and ideas of each other. We should be able to look at and understand our economic and social problems rationally. We should not mix these questions with religion.

facts.text: Regionalism means having excessive pride about one's region.
facts.quote: Regionalism means having excessive pride about one's region.

facts.text: Regionalism thrives on regional imbalance in development: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Punjab and Tamil Nadu developed, while Odisha, Bihar and Assam remained undeveloped economically and industrially.
facts.quote: Regionalism thrives on regional imbalance in development. ... States like Maharashtra, Gujarat, Punjab, Tamil Nadu developed economically and industrially; whereas States like Odisha, Bihar, Assam, remained undeveloped economically and industrially.

facts.text: The evil of regionalism can be tackled by reducing the imbalance in development.
facts.quote: The evil of regionalism can be tackled by reducing the imbalance in development.
